newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM palladium, silver tumble by daily limits.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM palladium, silver tumble by daily limits.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo palladium and silver futures closed sharply lower on Tuesday as most prices fell by their daily limits following a slide in spot prices, traders said.

Traders said there was talk that the Russian Platinum Group Metals Agency had offered to sell metals in the spot Zurich market on Monday, which helped pushed down spot palladium and yen-based Tokyo palladium prices.
"There is a feeling Russia is finally ready to resume PGM exports," one trader said. Benchmark June palladium fell by its 22 yen per gram daily limit to 520 yen.
Japanese traders expect Russian PGM shipments to Japan under long-term contracts to resume this week.
In palladium futures, private investors were mostly on the selling side, the traders said, adding the investors are keen to buy benchmark palladium at around the 500 yen level.
Most silver futures were glued to their limit lows for most of the day, following falls in spot silver prices. Benchmark April silver fell by its six yen per 10 grams daily limit to 158.1 yen.
Gold futures ended mostly marginally lower, while platinum ended lower on the heels of palladium, they said.
Bullion was quoted at $317.50/318.00 per ounce at 0742 GMT, against $318.20/318.70 in New York on Monday.
"Moderate physical demand in Asia supported spot gold earlier in the day, but gold turned weaker as physical buying ebbed, which dented Tokyo gold prices," one trader said.
Traders said, bearish sentiment on gold remained intact.
Gold futures ranged from five yen per gram lower to 21 yen firmer. Benchmark June ended one yen weaker at 1,145 yen.
Platinum futures ranged from four yen to 34 yen per gram lower. Benchmark June platinum was off 18 yen at 1,352 yen.
